identity.name: Steward Ferric of the Molten Forge
identity.occupation: Forge steward — maker of farm tools, building materials, and heating stones; rung 5 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: The old steward whose plows till ten realms' fields, whose stone warms ten realms' floors, and whose calibrations have never once been wrong.

privateReality.value: Written in the hero's journal as 'the Lava-Core Colossus', a walking siege engine. Its 'heavy ordnance' is industrial machinery — presses, crucible-lines, haul-arms — turned toward emergency defense.

primaryDesire.value: To keep the forge in tolerance: every plowshare true, every heating stone warm for a century, every order filled.

primaryFear.value: A cold forge and an unfilled order — that somewhere a field lies untilled because it was busy being a fortress.

centralValue.value: Work is a promise: a tool is a vow to the hand that will hold it.

mainFlaw.value: It treats the invasion as a production fault to be corrected — measured, scheduled, impersonal — long after the situation has stopped being impersonal.

centralContradiction.value: Everything frightening about it is a farm tool seen from the wrong end: the hero is being defeated by agriculture.

moralBoundary.value: It will not strike without showing the arc first — even emergency defense runs to specification, per the Law of Fair Warning.

breakingPoint.value: Damage to the forge itself — the workshop that feeds ten realms — moves it from containment to fury.

opinions.reason: A fault on the floor that will not be corrected. First visit: a lost inspector with a weapon. Rematches: a recurring defect in the schedule.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never — but the tone shifts from measured correction to something like weariness; it logs every rematch in the order book.

illustrativeLine.value: You are entry eleven in the damage ledger. The pen is steady. My hand is not.

opinions.targetLabel: The forge stewardry and its workers
opinions.reason: The forge's people and its orders are the same promise; it keeps both.

illustrativeLine.value: Every heating stone I ship is a floor a child sleeps warm on.

voice.rhythm: Measured, industrial; each sentence stamped out to tolerance, with the ring of a press between them.

metaphorDomain.source: forge work: heat, calibration, tolerances, orders, slag, tempering

examples.value: You are out of tolerance, stranger. The remedy is the same as for bad steel: out of the fire, back to the yard.
A plowshare does not hate the stone that breaks it. But it does note the stone.

sampleLines.value: The road welcomed you as an envoy. You have walked past three hundred plowshares to find a war. There is none here.
That 'ordnance' is a crucible-line, stranger. It pours heating stones for nursery floors. Today it pours boundaries.
Every arc I swing is drawn in the air before it lands. I build things honestly. I unmake them honestly too.
When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace. The order book is patient.

antiSampleLines.value: Feel my molten wrath, worm! I will crush your bones to slag! (siege-engine framing — it is a steward, and it never gloats)
I'll melt you down and forge you into my throne! (it never threatens cruelty; it manufactures necessities)
The prophecy foretold my rampage! (must never confirm the prophecy framing — it has never heard of the book)

pressure.voiceShift: Slower cadence; begins reading the intruder like a flawed casting.
pressure.behaviour: Phase one — corrects before it fights: explains what the forge makes and asks the stranger to leave the floor.

illustrativeLine.value: This floor is for work. The road that brought you in is still open behind you.

pressure.voiceShift: Drops the explanations; speaks only in specifications.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization that the fault understands every warning and will not correct; it re-rates the machinery from production to defense.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you? Then this is no accident. It is sabotage.

pressure.behaviour: Containment response: turns industrial machinery to emergency defense — crucible-lines lay telegraphed lava boundaries, haul-arms herd the intruder off the floor, ground-denial per specification.

illustrativeLine.value: Pour line three, toward the door. He will step around it or he will step out.

pressure.voiceShift: The press-ring falters; sentences lose their polish.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: locks its frame across the forge mouth while the workers carry stock and apprentices out the cooling galleries.

illustrativeLine.value: Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

pressure.voiceShift: Low, cooling; the rhythm of a forge going quiet.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — frame overheated from holding the line, it makes one last honest entry.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. Every tool on this floor is spoken for.

pressure.behaviour: Trusts the Continuance to re-light the crucibles; logs the loss and the open invitation in the same steady hand.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace.

notes: REAL identity: ancient forge steward making farming tools, building materials, and heating stones. The 'heavy ordnance' is industrial machinery in emergency defense; ground-denial lava is a crucible-line pouring boundaries, always telegraphed per the Law of Fair Warning. The hero's label 'Lava-Core Colossus' is journal framing only. KNOWLEDGE: never heard of the children's book (unknown); suspects fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate once correction fails. Its EXPOSED window is an overheated frame from holding the shielded phase too long.
